aggressive_definition: Advanced incident prostate cancer. The abstract separately analyzes nonadvanced incidence and prostate cancer mortality, but it does not report a total/general incident endpoint.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Cox proportional hazards regression was used to calculate HRs and 95% CIs of nonadvanced (n = 14,238) and advanced (n = 2,170) PCa incidence and PCa mortality (n = 760) during 1,729,896 person-years of follow-up.
study_design: Prospective cohort analysis in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study using recalled adolescent intake and subsequent prostate cancer follow-up.
reason: The abstract explicitly analyzes advanced PCa incidence, which is aggressive. It analyzes nonadvanced incidence separately but does not provide a total/general incident PCa endpoint. The analytic participant N is not stated in the abstract.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Positive trends were also observed for greater intakes of fruit juice (P-trend = 0.002), total fruit (P-trend = 0.014), and dark bread (P-trend = 0.035) with nonadvanced PCa risk and for greater intakes of legumes (P-trend < 0.001), fiber (P-trend = 0.001), and vegetable protein (P-trend = 0.013-0.040) with advanced PCa risk or PCa mortality.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row explicitly specifies advanced prostate cancer and uses the 2,170 advanced-case count.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: However, greater adolescent intakes of tomatoes (P-trend = 0.004) and nonstarch vegetables (P-trend = 0.025) were associated with reduced risk of nonadvanced PCa
